Our game list files Fire Kirin under the category Fish Game, and describes it as a fish shooting game. That is the fish table format: you sit at a cannon in a shared room, choose a bet per shot, and aim at targets that cross the screen. Small targets come up often, larger ones take more shots, and boss targets appear from time to time. Every shot costs your chosen bet whether it lands or not, and whether a target pays is decided by chance, not by aim alone.

If the format is new to you, what a fish table game is explains rooms, bet per shot and bosses in plain terms. We do not publish odds or RTP for any game, and we will not describe Fire Kirin's specific rooms or features until there is a version you can actually load here.

content:

Why this page no longer lists Panda Master tips

This page used to give boss strategies and multiplier tips and told readers to sign up for the game. Two problems: Panda Master is not available at Casinova, and nobody can honestly promise that a targeting trick works in a game whose outcomes are decided by chance. So the tips are gone. What is left is the status, what the game is, and the habits that are worth having in any fish game.

What Panda Master is

In our game list Panda Master sits in the category Fish Game and is described as a fish game app with colorful underwater tables. Fish games share one format: a shared room, a cannon, a bet you set per shot, and targets of different sizes crossing the screen. The fish table explainer covers the format, and the glossary defines the terms you will see in any of these apps.

Panda Master and Ultrapanda are two separate entries in our list. Both are coming soon, and one going live would not make the other loadable.

Practice on the closest live game

Juwa is live and is the fish specialist in the Casinova lineup: an app with slots and table-style games where the fish shooters are the main draw. Panda Master is a fish-first app too, which makes Juwa the nearest thing you can load. If you would rather have fish tables inside a small lobby with slots and keno, Gameroom is the second choice.

Fish table habits that transfer to any game

None of these change the odds. They change how long a balance lasts and how clearly you decide when to stop.

  1. Set the bet per shot before you sit down. Every shot costs the bet whether it lands or not. Fish tables ask for a decision every second, so a balance drains far faster at a high bet than the same balance does on slots. Choose a bet that gives you the session length you want.
  2. Decide a loss limit and a stop point in advance. Write down the amount you are prepared to lose and the balance at which you will leave. Deciding mid-session is when people raise bets to chase.
  3. Do not treat big targets as owed. A boss that has absorbed many shots is not "due". Each result is chance-based, and there is no reliable pattern to learn.
  4. Know your redeem numbers before the first shot. If you load $50 from your first deposit, the 100% match makes it $100 in the game. Redeem opens at 3x the load, $150, and caps at 8x, $400. Knowing the threshold gives you a concrete stop point.
  5. Take breaks. The pace of a shooter makes time pass quickly. A timer helps.

Our guide to playing Juwa well goes deeper on session rules and the redeem math, and it applies to fish tables generally. If you are not sure the shooter format is for you, fish table vs slots compares the two.

What will apply when Panda Master goes live

The platform rules are the same for every game, so they will be the same for Panda Master:

  • Deposits are by card only, into one Casinova wallet.
  • Loads are $5 to $500 each.
  • The deposit match is 100% on your first deposit and 50% on your second, applied at load, with nothing after that.
  • Redeem opens at 3x the load, is capped at 8x, needs an approved government ID and is reviewed by staff. There is no payout-time promise. See the ID verification guide.

The overview of coming-soon games lists the closest live game for each of the six.
